svg.title: Base-Case Revenue to $225,000 Owner Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-profit-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: Base-Case Revenue to $225,000 Owner Profit; subtitle: $500,000 retained operator revenue less $275,000 operating costs yields 45.0%.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Six bars contain an opening total, four signed deductions, and a closing total; the final bar is not another increment. Cost allocations are illustrative because only scenario totals are canonical. Opening gross revenue is gross within the operator income statement but already net of client subscription pass-through under the specified agency model.; caption: $500,000 − $120,000 − $75,000 − $50,000 − $30,000 = $225,000; $225,000 / $500,000 = 45.0%. Conservative is $100,000 revenue, $68,000 costs, and $32,000 profit at 32%. Scaled is $900,000 revenue, $378,000 costs, and $522,000 profit at 58%. The supplied monthly opex range of $1,500–$9,500 is not a ceiling on all-in annual scenario costs.; stages: label: Recognized retained revenue; value: $500,000 opening operator revenue total; numeric value: 500000.0; detail: Count earned partner spreads, master-agent residuals, GPO administrative rebates, and shared-savings fees. Exclude client software subscription principal and avoid applying a second retained-share reduction to this already-retained revenue.; label: Contractor delivery; value: −$120,000 annual delivery labor allocation; numeric value: -120000.0; detail: Allocate licensing operations, savings verification, and reconciliation work across the three contractor seats. This modeled deduction leaves $380,000 before remaining costs.; label: Acquisition and channel servicing; value: −$75,000 annual variable commercial costs; numeric value: -75000.0; detail: Budget qualified outreach, referral compensation, account onboarding, and partner-servicing costs without duplicating deductions already embedded in retained partner spreads.; label: Systems and professional operations; value: −$50,000 annual infrastructure operating allocation; numeric value: -50000.0; detail: Cover CRM, document storage, reconciliation tooling, bookkeeping, contract review, insurance, and operating administration. The modeled running balance becomes $255,000.; label: Credit and service-loss expense; value: −$30,000 annual modeled loss allocation; numeric value: -30000.0; detail: Model unrecovered customer exposure and service remediation as expenses. Revenue reversals already netted from the opening total must not also appear in this deduction.; label: Owner net profit; value: $225,000 closing profit at 45.0%; numeric value: 225000.0; detail: This is the canonical annual owner-profit endpoint, not another source of revenue. Personal taxes, financing choices, and owner distributions are not separately modeled.

rect.title: label: Recognized retained revenue; value: $500,000 opening operator revenue total; numeric value: 500000.0; detail: Count earned partner spreads, master-agent residuals, GPO administrative rebates, and shared-savings fees. Exclude client software subscription principal and avoid applying a second retained-share reduction to this already-retained revenue.

label: Contractor delivery; value: −$120,000 annual delivery labor allocation; numeric value: -120000.0; detail: Allocate licensing operations, savings verification, and reconciliation work across the three contractor seats. This modeled deduction leaves $380,000 before remaining costs.

label: Acquisition and channel servicing; value: −$75,000 annual variable commercial costs; numeric value: -75000.0; detail: Budget qualified outreach, referral compensation, account onboarding, and partner-servicing costs without duplicating deductions already embedded in retained partner spreads.

label: Systems and professional operations; value: −$50,000 annual infrastructure operating allocation; numeric value: -50000.0; detail: Cover CRM, document storage, reconciliation tooling, bookkeeping, contract review, insurance, and operating administration. The modeled running balance becomes $255,000.

label: Credit and service-loss expense; value: −$30,000 annual modeled loss allocation; numeric value: -30000.0; detail: Model unrecovered customer exposure and service remediation as expenses. Revenue reversals already netted from the opening total must not also appear in this deduction.

label: Owner net profit; value: $225,000 closing profit at 45.0%; numeric value: 225000.0; detail: This is the canonical annual owner-profit endpoint, not another source of revenue. Personal taxes, financing choices, and owner distributions are not separately modeled.
